flagship.headline: Parlophone releases Beatles for Sale in the UK
flagship.summary_line_1: Parlophone released the Beatles' fourth studio album Beatles for Sale in the UK on December 4, 1964, per the Beatles Bible.
flagship.summary_line_2: It spent 11 weeks at No. 1 on the UK albums chart, per This Day in Music, and the clip below is Eight Days a Week.

events.headline: Jay-Z is born in Brooklyn
events.summary_line_1: Shawn Corey Carter, later known as Jay-Z, was born in a Brooklyn housing project on December 4, 1969, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: He went on to co-found Roc-A-Fella Records, and the clip below is Hard Knock Life.

events.headline: Hendrix drives his Flying V into his amps at Newcastle City Hall
events.summary_line_1: The Jimi Hendrix Experience played the City Hall in Newcastle on December 4, 1967, on the penultimate night of a 16-date UK package tour that also featured Pink Floyd, The Move and The Nice, per This Day in Music.
events.summary_line_2: Frustrated by equipment problems, Hendrix rammed his Gibson Flying V into his speaker cabinets, and some accounts say it stuck in the amp, and the clip below is Purple Haze.

events.headline: The Byrds hit No. 1 with Turn! Turn! Turn!
events.summary_line_1: The Byrds' Turn! Turn! Turn! (To Everything There Is a Season) reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the chart dated December 4, 1965, per Stereogum.
events.summary_line_2: It stayed on top for three weeks as the band's second No. 1, with Pete Seeger's Ecclesiastes adaptation as the lyric, and the clip below is the single.

events.headline: The Beatles play two shows at Newcastle City Hall
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two concerts at the City Hall in Newcastle on December 4, 1965, after a tough drive through snow, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their fourth and last performance at the venue, and the 11-song set opened with I Feel Fine, which is the clip below.

events.headline: Parlophone releases Beatles for Sale in the UK
events.summary_line_1: Parlophone released the Beatles' fourth studio album Beatles for Sale in the UK on December 4, 1964, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It spent 11 weeks at No. 1 on the UK albums chart, per This Day in Music, and the clip below is Eight Days a Week.

events.headline: The Beatles appear on Tuesday Rendezvous at Wembley
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles mimed Love Me Do and P.S. I Love You for the ITV children's show Tuesday Rendezvous at Wembley Studios on December 4, 1962, per Wikipedia and the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: It was their first London TV appearance, and the clip below is P.S. I Love You.

events.headline: The BBC broadcasts The Beatles on The Talent Spot
events.summary_line_1: The BBC Light Programme broadcast the Beatles on The Talent Spot from 5 to 5:30 pm on December 4, 1962, with Love Me Do, P.S. I Love You and Twist and Shout, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: The performance was recorded on November 27, a week before it aired, and the clip below is Love Me Do.
